calls.head: Strength in numbers for the Islanders
calls.body: The Islanders roll four lines, but the Sharks lean on their top six. The Islanders are one of the league’s best for depth, and San Jose is near the bottom. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Islanders.
calls.call: The Islanders spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Sharks.

calls.beyond: San Jose usually uses their bottom six less than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a short bench: the bottom six played 35% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Stenberg wins it in a shootout
paras: Ben Hutton scored his first goal for the Islanders early in the first to open the scoring. Ivar Stenberg made it 1-1 for San Jose late in the period, and Victor Eklund restored the Isles’ lead on the power play early in the second. Tyler Toffoli made it 2-2 for San Jose midway through the period. Two fights broke out at once late in the period, and Barclay Goodrow, Mitchell Chaffee, Ty Dellandrea and Kyle MacLean all got five for fighting. Stenberg scored the only goal of the shootout for the Sharks.

The Sharks had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Islanders 41-32. Yaroslav Askarov settled in after a shaky start for the Sharks: he gave up two goals on the first nine shots, then stopped the last 23, and Ilya Sorokin, who gave up five goals against New Jersey in his last start, made 39 saves in a losing effort.
Mason Marchment took three penalties on his own. The Sharks improved to 8-11-1, sixth in the Pacific, while the Islanders dropped to 7-6-4, fifth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Sharks won for the first time in six games.
The Islanders are winless in four (0-2-2).
The Sharks’ Alexander Wennberg was back in the lineup after missing ten games.
Victor Eklund has scored in three straight games.
